guideTitle: The Best Office Chairs for Tall People Who Need More Seat and Back
breadcrumbLabel: Best Office Chairs for Tall People
metaTitle: Best Office Chairs for Tall People: High Seats and Tall Backs (2026)
metaDescription: We compared office chairs for tall users on maximum seat height, back height, seat depth adjustment and weight capacity, from budget mesh chairs to Steelcase.
introParagraphs: For a tall person, the first problem with most office chairs is simple geometry: the seat does not go high enough, the seat pan is too short for longer thighs, and the backrest stops below the shoulder blades. Padding and styling matter far less than whether the chair reaches the right height at your desk.

That makes the top of the seat-height range, seat depth adjustment and back height the numbers to compare first. The chairs in this guide top out between 20 and 22 inches on the budget and mid-range side, while the Steelcase chairs are configured to order and add more adjustment and much longer warranties.

Our comparison is based on published specifications, adjustment ranges, warranty terms and price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $120 to just over $1,700 at the time of writing.

gtplayer-gaming-chair-tall.badge: Best Budget Pick With the Highest Seat
gtplayer-gaming-chair-tall.summary: A 22-inch maximum seat height and a 300 lb rating for under $200.
gtplayer-gaming-chair-tall.description:
The GTPLAYER is the low-cost choice when seat height is the priority: its 18.5- to 22-inch range tops out higher than any other budget or mid-range chair here.

The listing also gives a 300 lb capacity, a 90- to 160-degree recline and a retractable footrest, which suits reclining between tasks. Lumbar and head support come from pillows rather than an adjustable mechanism, so fit depends on where the pillows sit on your back.

It is a gaming-style chair in PU leather, which looks out of place in some offices and holds more heat than mesh. If you want mesh and adjustable lumbar at a similar price, the SIHOO M57 tops out only slightly lower, at 21.7 inches.
pros: Highest maximum seat height among the non-Steelcase picks
cons: Pillow lumbar rather than adjustable support
PU leather is less breathable than mesh
Gaming styling may not suit a professional office
gtplayer-gaming-chair-tall.bestFor: Tall users on a budget who need the highest possible seat and like to recline.
gtplayer-gaming-chair-tall.skipIf: You want breathable mesh or adjustable lumbar; the SIHOO M57 offers both for a similar price.

sihoo-m57-ergonomic-tall.summary: A high mesh back, adjustable lumbar and 3D armrests at a mid-range price.
sihoo-m57-ergonomic-tall.description:
The SIHOO M57 is the most complete mesh chair here for under $200, pairing a high mesh back with adjustable lumbar, an adjustable headrest and 3D armrests.

For a tall user, the high back and adjustable headrest are the practical advantages over the cheaper Marsail and the similarly priced GTPLAYER. The 3D armrests also help when you raise the seat and need the arms to follow.

The seat range tops out at 21.7 inches, so the tallest users at a standard desk may still find it low. The listing does not mention seat depth adjustment; for that, the SIHOO Doro C300 is the step up.
pros: High mesh back with an adjustable headrest
cons: 21.7-inch maximum may be low for the tallest users
sihoo-m57-ergonomic-tall.bestFor: Tall users who want a breathable high-back chair with adjustable lumbar and arms for under $200.
sihoo-m57-ergonomic-tall.skipIf: Seat depth is your main fit problem; the SIHOO Doro C300 lists seat depth adjustment.

sihoo-b100-tall.summary: A high mesh back, headrest and adjustable lumbar for about $160.
sihoo-b100-tall.description:
The SIHOO B100 covers the tall-user basics for less than the M57: a high mesh back, a headrest, adjustable lumbar and a three-year warranty.

The savings come from the armrests, which are 2D rather than 3D, and a slightly lower maximum seat height of 21 inches. For someone who mainly needs a taller backrest, those may be acceptable trade-offs.

If you are near the top of the height range, the extra 0.7 inches on the M57, or the 22 inches on the GTPLAYER, may matter more than the price difference.
pros: High backrest for a longer torso
Three-year warranty at a lower price
sihoo-b100-tall.bestFor: Tall users who mainly need a taller mesh back and adjustable lumbar at a moderate price.
sihoo-b100-tall.skipIf: You need the seat to go above 21 inches; the GTPLAYER or SIHOO M57 go higher.

marsail-ergonomic-tall.summary: The lowest-priced high-back mesh chair here, with adjustable lumbar and flip-up arms.
marsail-ergonomic-tall.description:
The Marsail is the cheapest way into a high-back mesh chair with adjustable lumbar and a headrest, at about $120 at the time of writing.

The weak point for a tall buyer is seat height. At 16.5 to 20 inches, it has the lowest maximum in this guide, so it suits people whose height is mostly in the torso, or who use a lower desk, better than long-legged users. Flip-up arms let it tuck under a desk but offer little adjustment, and the warranty is one year.

If you can stretch to about $160, the SIHOO B100 adds an extra inch of seat height and a three-year warranty.
pros: Flip-up arms tuck under a desk
cons: Lowest maximum seat height in this guide
marsail-ergonomic-tall.bestFor: Buyers with a longer torso, or a lower desk, who need a high mesh back for as little as possible.
marsail-ergonomic-tall.skipIf: You have long legs; a 20-inch maximum seat height is likely to be too low.

sihoo-doro-c300-tall.summary: The only non-Steelcase pick here that lists seat depth adjustment, plus a self-adjusting backrest.
sihoo-doro-c300-tall.description:
The SIHOO Doro C300 is the budget-to-mid-range pick for tall users with longer thighs, because it is the only chair under $1,000 here that lists seat depth adjustment.

SIHOO describes an auto-following backrest that moves with you and a suspended mesh back. Those are manufacturer design claims; the more concrete advantage is the sliding seat, which lets longer legs get support closer to the knee.

At about $300 it costs noticeably more than the other SIHOO chairs, and the 21.7-inch maximum seat height is the same as the M57's.
pros: Seat depth adjustment for longer thighs
cons: Costs more than the other SIHOO picks
Maximum seat height no higher than the M57's
sihoo-doro-c300-tall.bestFor: Tall users whose thighs extend past the front of a standard seat and who want to stay around $300.
sihoo-doro-c300-tall.skipIf: Your main problem is seat height rather than depth; the GTPLAYER goes higher for less.

steelcase-gesture-tall.summary: Configurable seat height, seat depth adjustment and a 12-year warranty.
steelcase-gesture-tall.description:
The Steelcase Gesture is the chair to consider if you want to configure a chair around your height rather than fit yourself to a fixed range: Steelcase offers it with extended cylinder options, and it adjusts seat height and depth.

Its LiveBack design and 360-degree arms are the distinguishing features; the arms are designed to follow you when you work on a phone or tablet as well as a keyboard. The 12-year warranty is also far longer than anything under $1,000 here.

The price, about $1,510 at the time of writing, is the obvious barrier, and the tall-user benefit depends on ordering the right cylinder. Check the configuration before buying.
cons: Tall-user fit depends on the configuration ordered
steelcase-gesture-tall.bestFor: Tall users who want a configurable chair with seat depth adjustment and a long warranty.
steelcase-gesture-tall.skipIf: You recline often and want head support; the Gesture with headrest adds an adjustable headrest.

steelcase-leap-v2-tall.summary: Independent lower-back firmness, seat edge adjustment and a 12-year warranty.
steelcase-leap-v2-tall.description:
The Steelcase Leap V2 is the premium pick if lower-back adjustment matters more than arm movement: Steelcase lets you set lower-back firmness and upper-back force separately.

It also lists seat edge adjustment and height- and width-adjustable arms, and carries the same 12-year warranty as the Gesture for somewhat less at the time of writing.

There is no headrest, which is a real consideration for tall users whose head sits above a standard backrest, and the listing does not give a seat height range, so check it against your desk.
steelcase-leap-v2-tall.bestFor: Tall users who want fine lumbar adjustment and a long warranty and do not need a headrest.
steelcase-leap-v2-tall.skipIf: You want head support; the Gesture with headrest is the Steelcase option for that.

steelcase-gesture-headrest-tall.summary: The Gesture with an adjustable headrest for head and neck support.
steelcase-gesture-headrest-tall.description:
The Gesture with headrest is the same chair as the standard Gesture with an adjustable headrest added, and it is the option to choose if your head sits above the top of a typical backrest.

The headrest adjusts for height and angle, which matters most for tall users who recline. Everything else, including the LiveBack, 360-degree arms and 12-year warranty, matches the standard Gesture.

It is the most expensive chair here at about $1,720 at the time of writing, roughly $200 more than the standard Gesture. If you rarely lean back, the headrest may not justify that difference.
pros: Same adjustment and warranty as the Gesture
steelcase-gesture-headrest-tall.bestFor: Tall users who recline often and want head support on a configurable premium chair.
steelcase-gesture-headrest-tall.skipIf: You sit upright most of the time; the standard Gesture costs less.

buyingCriteria.criterion: Maximum seat height against your desk
buyingCriteria.explanation:
A chair's range only matters relative to your desk. If the seat tops out too low, your knees end up above your hips however good the chair is otherwise.

Here, maximums run from 20 inches (Marsail) to 22 inches (GTPLAYER); the Steelcase Gesture offers extended cylinder options. Measure your desk and compare it with the top of each range.

Longer thighs often extend past a standard seat, leaving the back of the knee unsupported or forcing you away from the backrest. The SIHOO Doro C300 and the Steelcase chairs list seat depth or seat edge adjustment; the others do not.
A tall torso may reach past the top of a standard backrest. High-back mesh chairs and headrests help; the Leap V2 is the one premium pick without a headrest.
We would choose a chair rated comfortably above your weight. Only some listings here state a capacity; the GTPLAYER lists 300 lb.
"Adjustable" can mean very different things. 2D arms move up and down; 3D arms also move in and out or pivot. Check the number of adjustments, not just the word.

faq.q: What seat height do I need if I'm tall?
faq.a: It depends on your leg length and desk height more than your overall height. A common guideline is feet flat on the floor, thighs roughly level and elbows near desk height. Measure from the floor to the back of your knee while seated in shoes, and choose a chair whose maximum is comfortably above that.

faq.q: Is a gaming chair or an ergonomic office chair better for tall users?
faq.a: It depends on what you need. In this guide, the GTPLAYER gaming chair has the highest maximum seat height of the non-Steelcase picks and a deep recline, while the mesh chairs offer more breathable backs and adjustable lumbar. Compare seat height, seat depth and adjustment rather than the category label.

faq.q: Do I need a footrest with a tall office chair?
faq.a: Usually the problem for tall users is the opposite: the chair is too low. A footrest is more useful if your desk is set high and your feet do not reach the floor with the seat at the right height.

faq.q: How do I pair a tall office chair with a standing desk?
faq.a: Set the desk's sitting height so your elbows are near desk height with the chair adjusted for your legs, then save it as a preset if the desk allows. See our [standing desk for tall person](/guide/best-standing-desk-for-tall-person) guide for desk options.

bottomLine: On a budget, the choice is mostly about seat height. The GTPLAYER goes highest at 22 inches, the SIHOO M57 is the better-equipped mesh chair just below that, and the Marsail saves money but tops out at 20 inches, which may rule it out for long-legged users. The SIHOO Doro C300 is the one to consider if seat depth, not height, is the problem.

The Steelcase chairs are worth paying more for if you want configuration options and a 12-year warranty. Choose the Gesture for configurable height and 360-degree arms, add the headrest if you recline, or choose the Leap V2 for finer lower-back adjustment.
